home.intro_text:
This is the third straight season I've written my guide and this version is by far the best yet. I've spent countless hours studying every team so I can give us the best chance of making money this season.

If you're just discovering me, the main thing you need to know is that absolutely everything I post is free. Here's a glimpse at what I'll be sharing with you throughout the NFL season…
features: Parlays, Flyers and Best Bets for every game week
Data Sheets to help you pick your own winners
Algorithms to identify the best matchups
home.closing_text: Whether you're a bettor, a fantasy football player or simply an NFL fan, this guide will give you more knowledge than all your buddies going into the 2025 season. Hope you enjoy it.
home.title: WELCOME TO MY NFL BETTING GUIDE 2026

teams.defence: The Ravens’ defense fell off last season, especially in the pass rush. They placed 28th overall in both team pass rush win rate and sacks (30 total) in 2025. Enter Trey Hendrickson and Calais Campbell this year and that bottom-five defense should be back to top-10 territory. Rookie linebacker Zion Young should also help in that area. Their secondary is one of the best in the league, led by Kyle Hamilton, Malaki Starks and Chidobe Awuzie. If everything clicks in Jesse Minter’s new scheme, the Ravens will have a very good defense.
teams.future_text: Flowers just signed a massive four-year, $140 million contract with $108 million guaranteed. He produced 1211 yards last year and 1059 the year before, despite Lamar Jackson dealing with some injuries. There isn’t much competition in this receiver room and he should comfortably clear this mark again.
teams.receivers: The Ravens lost tight end Isaiah Likely to the Giants which means veteran Mark Andrews regains the role as TE1. Andrews is still only 30 years old and the Ravens will hope he can recapture the form he showed back in 2021 and 2022 where he had 70+ receptions both years. They also signed Durham Smythe as backup tight end who is a serviceable option. At wide receiver, Zay Flowers is the undisputed WR1 and is coming off back to back Pro Bowl seasons. He had 1200 receiving yards last year along with 5 TDs. Flowers just signed a huge extension in the off season which will make him one of the highest paid receivers in the NFL. I don’t think he’s rated in those top receivers, so maybe he will have a point to prove to get himself there. There have been a lot of positive reports coming out about rookie WR Ja’Kobi Lane who was drafted with pick 80. He is an athletic beast at over 6 foot 3 and could have an increased role as the season progresses.
teams.overview: The Ravens are currently fourth favorite to win the Super Bowl, proving that Vegas is keen on them to be a good team again. I definitely rate them, but I just can’t see this team winning the Super Bowl in all honesty. Derrick Henry is getting older and Lamar is still elite, but he has dealt with quite a few injuries in recent years. Losing C Danny Pinton to season-ending injury is tough and may lead to early offensive struggles for the Ravens. They’ll need big improvements defensively compared to last season and they did hire former Chargers’ DC Jesse Minter as head coach. Baltimore's 2026 win total forecast is at 11.5, tied for the NFL's highest mark, reflecting the belief that a healthy Lamar Jackson plus a retooled defense returns this roster to true contender status after last year's uneven, injury-shortened finish to the season, when Jackson missed four total games and the pass rush ranked among the league's very worst.
teams.running_backs: Derrick Henry is still the workhorse RB for the Ravens, but the big question is how long he can maintain his elite efficiency. Henry will turn 33 this season and he’s had 300+ carries in back-to-back years with the Ravens. He’s going to regress at some point, but they’ll be hoping he can produce again this season. Henry had 1595 rushing yards last year with 16 rushing TDs, another incredible season. He did have some fumble issues though, losing the ball a career-high 3 times last year. No back with 100-plus carries has topped 4.5 yards per carry at age 35-plus since 2016, but Henry still has a couple of years before he gets there. Justice Hill remains the third-down and change of pace back behind Henry. There isn’t a lot of depth in this backfield but the Ravens are relying on Henry to maintain his performance going into his 11th NFL season.
teams.quarterbacks: Lamar Jackson is still the heartbeat of this team and Baltimore will be hoping he can get back to his best after an injury-riddled 2025 campaign. Lamar started 13 games last season but was clearly not at full health, ending the year with 21 passing TDs and just 2 rushing TDs. They were clearly protecting him at points last season, with Derrick Henry taking most of the goal line carries and far less frequent designed run plays for Lamar. Lamar is still just 29 years old and in his prime, so I expect him to return to the MVP conversation if he stays healthy. Tyler Huntley signed a two year deal and will remain as the backup. He’s one of the better backups in the league in my opinion.
teams.name: BALTIMORE RAVENS
teams.offseason_changes: Baltimore had a clear focus to improve defensively, and they’ve added 10 Pro Bowls of pass rusher experience between Trey Hendrickson and Calais Campbell, then drafted Zion Young 45th overall. The Ravens actually traded for 5x Pro Bowler Maxx Crosby but the deal then fell through after a failed medical. They also signed new head coach Jesse Minter, previously the Chargers’ DC. The Chargers finished in the top 10 in sacks in both Minter’s seasons as DC.
teams.prediction_text: I have the Ravens narrowly winning the AFC North over the Bengals. I think the Steelers will be slightly less competitive but the Ravens should return to the top of the division with better health and a revamped defense.

teams.defence: The Bengals have completely revamped their defense and their season will likely come down to how it performs. Dexter Lawrence anchors the interior after arriving via trade and he gives them a serious force up front for the first time in years. The additions of Boye Mafe and Jonathan Allen give Cincinnati proven pass-rush and run-stopping experience too. Bryan Cook is a solid safety and fills the missing piece next to Jordan Battle. They’ve also got a young core of Shemar Stewart, DJ Turner II and Barrett Carter who should benefit from the veteran experience around them.
teams.future_text: Burrow has cleared this mark in three of his six NFL seasons, but they are all seasons where he was fully healthy. Basically if he plays a full season, he clears this. All reports are that he is in great shape and feeling motivated.
teams.receivers: This is one of the most stacked receiver rooms in the NFL, led by arguably the best receiver in the league, Ja’Marr Chase. He’s put up over 1000 receiving yards in all five of his seasons as a pro and is coming off a 1412 yard season with 8 TDs. Chase is the second-highest paid receiver in the league, earning over $40 million per season. There’s not much more that needs to be said about him, he’s an elite weapon for Joe Burrow and he can do it all. Tee Higgins would be WR1 on a lot of other teams but plays second fiddle to Chase. Higgins had a down year by his standards in 2025, finishing with just one game of 100+ yards. Andrei Iosivas, Mitchell Tinsley and tight end Mike Gesicki all complement the two stars nicely. Expect big numbers from this unit in 2026, especially if Burrow stays healthy and their defense can get them on the field more often.
teams.overview: The Bengals went all-in on defense this offseason, spending over $126 million to add safety Bryan Cook, edge rusher Boye Mafe, defensive lineman Jonathan Allen, and traded for former Giants defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence — moves made possible partly by Joe Burrow restructuring his contract. Last season, Cincinnati's defense couldn't get stops, forcing Burrow to play from behind often and limiting a dangerous offense that still finished with the fourth-fewest rushing yards per game (93.6). This year, Burrow is healthy, fully loaded, and a top-four MVP favorite, with Chase Brown entrenched as RB1 after a breakout season and Ja'Marr Chase leading one of the NFL's best receiver rooms. Tee Higgins and Mike Gesicki add further depth. With a revamped front seven featuring Lawrence, Mafe, and Allen alongside young talents like Shemar Stewart, the defense should finally support the offense.
teams.running_backs: The Bengals had the fourth fewest rushing yards per game in 2025 with just 93.6 per game. Some of that comes down to game script, where they were often playing from behind. It’s also a pass-heavy team with Joe Burrow at QB. Chase Brown is the undisputed RB1 after a breakout 2025 season. He had 1019 rushing yards along with 437 receiving yards and 11 total touchdowns for the year. Despite being a smaller back he’s super explosive and can damage teams on the ground and through the air. This will be the final year of his rookie contract, so he’s got plenty of motivation to perform and earn himself a pay rise. I think Brown is set for a massive season and his high price in fantasy drafts reflects that. His season rushing line is set at 825.5 yards which is very low but I also like his receiving props. Samaje Perine is the more bulldozing back and is often used in short yardage situations. The Bengals are clearly happy with their offense and that’s reflected with the lack of changes over the off-season.
teams.quarterbacks: When Burrow is healthy, he is a top QB in the NFL. In four of his past five seasons, more than 6% of his total pass attempts have been touchdowns. Most other QBs are in the 4-4.5% range. Burrow is currently the fourth favorite for MVP and it’s hard to argue against him having a great season. The Bengals’ defense could barely get a stop last year which often meant Burrow was forced to play from behind or not be on the field for long periods. That should change this year and will allow Burrow to cook. He is fully healthy and stacked with talent around him. I wouldn’t be surprised if he returns to the heights of 2024 where he had 43 TD passes and nearly 5000 passing yards. He’s in his prime at 29 years old and the Bengals are going all-in. Joe Flacco returns as arguably the best backup in the NFL. Despite his age he can still sling it. The Bengals will be hoping he won’t be required though…
teams.name: CINCINNATI BENGALS
teams.offseason_changes: The Bengals finally took some action to improve their defense, which has been a handbrake on their last few seasons. They spent over $126 million in new contracts, landing safety Bryan Cook, edge rusher Boye Mafe and defensive lineman Jonathan Allen. Then they doubled down and landed former Giants’ defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence. All this spending was helped by Joe Burrow restructuring his contract to free up some cap space. The offense remained largely untouched and we know that they can put up scores when all healthy.
teams.prediction_text: I have the Bengals making the playoffs but narrowly missing out on the AFC North title to the Ravens. It’s really all on their defense this year, if they can make some good improvements then this team will win more games. Who knows how long they’ll be able to keep this offense together?

teams.defence: Defense wasn’t the issue for the Browns last year, with one of the highest rated units in the league. Unfortunately they lost both their best player Myles Garrett and their defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz. The bombshell trade with Garrett did bring Jared Verse to Cleveland and he’s an exciting prospect, recording 7.5 sacks for the Rams last season. He’s just 25 years old and is a nice replacement at defensive end. The Browns are still stacked with talent, with the likes of Denzel Ward, Tyson Campbell, Carson Schwesinger and Mason Graham. This should still be a top-15 defense but it’s going to be a big task replacing a coordinator and reining DPOTY in the same off-season.
teams.future_text: Concepcion has been all the buzz in training camp and I think he will be WR1 over Jerry Jeudy pretty quickly. With the Brown’s likely behind in most games, they’re probably going to have to throw the ball. Concepcion is a first round pick and should be able to show his talent immediately.
teams.receivers: The Browns had just two players with more than 600 receiving yards in 2025 – rookie tight end Harold Fannin Jr (731 yards) and WR Jerry Jeudy (602). They’ve gone heavy in the draft to improve their receiver room, taking WR KC Concepcion with pick 24 and WR Denzel Boston with pick 39. They’re both exciting prospects with Concepcion averaging 15.1 yards per catch and 9 touchdowns at Texas A&M last season. Boston had 881 yards and 11 touchdowns for Washington in his final college year too. Tight end Harold Fannin Jr looks like a foundational piece and he’ll be thrown into an even bigger role now that David Njoku is gone. The talent is there now for the Browns, but the bigger issue here is who throws them the ball. I’d avoid betting on their props until we get a better idea of who is starting QB and how they gel in pre-season.
teams.overview: The Browns overhauled their coaching staff, replacing Kevin Stefanski with Todd Monken, and shocked the league by trading star pass-rusher Myles Garrett to the Rams for Jared Verse and draft capital, also losing defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz in the process. Last season, Cleveland struggled offensively with the second-fewest passing yards per game and a bottom-six rushing attack, though their defense ranked among the league's best. This year, Deshaun Watson returns from injury to compete with Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel for the starting job, while Quinshon Judkins looks to build on a promising rookie season after a serious leg injury. The Browns invested heavily in receivers, drafting KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston to support tight end Harold Fannin Jr. Verse should help offset Garrett's absence, but replacing a Defensive Player of the Year is tough.
teams.running_backs: The Browns’ rushing attack was sixth-worst in the NFL last season, but Quinshon Judkins emerged as a solid prospect throughout the season. He suffered a pretty horrific fractured leg and dislocated ankle in December but is reportedly healthy and ready to go for this season. Prior to his injury he had 827 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns which had him in contention for OROTY. The worrying thing was that he averaged just 3.6 yards per carry, but a lot of that came down to the Browns’ weak offensive line and poor passing game. Dylan Sampson will remain RB2, he had some serviceable games last year but actually had more receiving yards (271) than rushing yards (175).
teams.quarterbacks: The Browns had the second-fewest passing yards per game last season and the big question here is who will start Week 1. Head coach Todd Monken hasn’t given much away so far but it’s likely to be either Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders to take the reins. Watson has recovered from his achilles tear that wiped out his whole 2025 season and it’s his last chance to prove himself in the last year of his contract. He restructured his deal which freed up $36 million in cap space for the Browns. Shedeur Sanders is a fan favorite and led the Browns to a few wins last year, but his 7-10 TD to interception ratio wasn’t overly convincing. Dillon Gabriel started six games in his rookie season but it seems he’s third in the pecking order going into 2026.
teams.name: CLEVELAND BROWNS
teams.offseason_changes: Big changes all over the place for the Browns after firing Kevin Stefanski and replacing him with Todd Monken as head coach. The bombshell trade of the off-season was sending Myles Garrett to the Rams for Jared Verse and a load of draft capital. He’s a massive loss for this defense, as well as defensive coordinator Jim Schwartz who resigned after missing out on the head coaching job. Deshaun Watson should be healthy and he’ll be in a three-way quarterback competition with Shedeur Sanders and Dillon Gabriel. The Browns invested heavily in their offense through the draft, taking two receivers in the first two rounds and OT Spencer Fano with pick 9.
teams.prediction_text: Another tough year ahead for the Browns in my opinion. This will be Deshaun Watson’s final year of his contract but I wouldn’t be surprised to see at least three different starting QBs throughout the year. Their defense is not as good without Garrett and they’ll struggle to win too many games.

teams.defence: The defense remains the backbone of this team despite Mike Tomlin’s departure. Cornerback Jamel Dean will be a nice addition to the secondary, which already added Jalen Ramsey via trade last season. Dean arrives on the second-largest free agent contract in franchise history. The defense is now looking stacked, with Alex Highsmith leading the pass rush, alongside Cam Heyward, TJ Watt and Patrick Queen. This defense was what won the Steelers their division last season and they’ve arguably improved. They’ll be the key once again to masking some of their offensive limitations.
teams.future_text: I’m really not liking Rodgers output for this season. He had such a low average depth of pass last year and while they now have Michael Pittman, I’m not sure how much he can improve at this age. There is always an injury risk for him too, he doesn’t move well and could get hit a lot this season.
teams.receivers: Pittsburgh made a receiver trade for the second straight year, bringing in Michael Pittman from the Colts on a three year, $59 million deal after doing similar for DK Metcalf in 2025. Pittman looks like a good fit for where this passing game lives – short options. He averaged just 8.1 air yards per target in his best season, which lines up nicely with Rodgers’ increasingly short-range approach in the later stages of his career. DK Metcalf should still be WR1 and is the deeper threat to pair with Pittman’s skill set underneath. Roman Wilson rounds out the receiving group and the Steelers also have two solid tight ends in Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington. The concern here isn’t the talent, it’s improving on a passing game that was 21st in success rate and 16th in EPA per play last season. The QB situation is the same, so we’ll see if Mike McCarthy and Rodgers can improve on last year’s numbers.
teams.overview: The Steelers brought back Aaron Rodgers for what he's announced will be his final NFL season, while making a major change at head coach — Mike McCarthy replaces Mike Tomlin after his 19-year tenure. Pittsburgh also traded for receiver Michael Pittman to pair with DK Metcalf and added cornerback Jamel Dean in a huge free-agent deal. Last season, the Steelers won their division largely on the back of a strong defense, though their passing attack ranked poorly in efficiency, with Rodgers throwing an unusually high rate of short passes. This year, Rico Dowdle joins Jaylen Warren in a solid backfield, while Metcalf and Pittman give Rodgers reliable short-range targets. The defense remains stacked with TJ Watt, Cam Heyward, and now Dean anchoring the secondary.
teams.running_backs: The Steelers lost Kenneth Gainwell in free agency but replaced him with former Panthers’ and Cowboys’ RB Rico Dowdle. Dowdle has back to back seasons with 1000+ rushing yards and had a couple of massive games last year with 206 yards and 183 yards in back to back weeks. His efficiency dipped later in the season but he’s probably an upgrade on Gainwell. Dowdle will be fighting for the starting RB position with Jaylen Warren. Warren had a very solid 2025 campaign, putting up 958 rushing yards and 333 receiving yards. He was Rodgers’ favorite dump-off option last year with 2+ targets in all but two games. This should be a solid backfield and I expect the Steelers to lean on the run a lot this season with Rodgers being more of a game manager. They might run with the hot hand at times and see who is performing better week to week.
teams.quarterbacks: Aaron Rodgers returns for his final NFL season on a one-year deal worth up to $25 million. The Steelers placed an unrestricted free-agent tender on him to keep the door closed to other teams. Rodgers still has a decent arm and recorded 3,322 passing yards last season to go with 24 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. The worrying stat for Rodgers and the Steelers is that 76% of his attempts travelled under 10 yards last season – the highest rate in the league. It’ll be interesting to see if Mike McCarthy trusts him to air it out more this season. He does have two really solid receivers in Metcalf and Pittman at his disposal. Rodgers wants to win one more Super Bowl but I really don’t see that happening this year. Mason Rudolph returns as the backup QB and whilst he’s been serviceable, he’s not going to set the world on fire if he gets starting reps.
teams.name: PITTSBURGH STEELERS
teams.offseason_changes: Pittsburgh spent the off-season publicly courting Aaron Rodgers to run it back for one more season, and they succeeded. He’s announced this will be his final year in the NFL. The big change is at head coach – with Mike McCarthy taking the reins after Mike Tomlin stepped down after 19 seasons with the team. McCarthy has over 290 wins in the NFL and coached the Packers (with Rodgers as QB) between 2006-2018 and the Cowboys between 2020-2024. The Steelers also traded for veteran receiver Michael Pittman and he’ll be a nice addition alongside DK Metcalf. Defensively, they added cornerback Jamel Dean in one of their largest free-agent contracts ever.
teams.prediction_text: I think it’ll be a year of slight regression for the Steelers. They have a decent roster and their defense is always scary, but Mike Tomlin is gone and it’s a period of change. I don’t think Aaron Rodgers has the ability to win them games with his own arm anymore.

teams.defence: The Bills had a great rushing attack, but their rushing defense was in the bottom-five, allowing 5 yards per carry. Their secondary was elite, allowing the fewest passing yards per game (156.9) but part of that was because teams knew they could run all over them. Jim Leonhard’s 3-4 scheme was elite against the run in Denver and he has a big task to improve Buffalo’s run defense this season. Bradley Chubb and second-round rookie TJ Parker should improve the pass rush as well, while Ed Oliver anchors the interior after an injury-shortened 2025.
teams.future_text: Cook scored 12 rushing TDs last year and 16 the year before. He’s had two breakout years and there isn’t anyone challenging him for the RB1 role. With the Bills expected to be good again, Cook should get plenty of opportunities at the goal line.
teams.receivers: The Bills have a solid three-man wide receiver rotation for the first time in years after adding DJ Moore. Khalil Shakir had a solid season in 2025 with 719 receiving yards but he’s not really a first option receiver. Keon Coleman is a former second-round pick but just hasn’t delivered on his potential so far. He had 112 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 last year, but then never had a game with more than 49 yards after that point. He was also a healthy scratch for a couple of games as the Bills lost trust in him. DJ Moore is going to be crucial for Allen but it remains to be seen if he’s a complete fix to their passing game problems. Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox are great options at tight end, I’m a big fan of Kincaid especially who looks to be healthier coming into this season. He dealt with a PCL injury over the past year or so.
teams.overview: The Bills enter a new era with Joe Brady replacing Sean McDermott as head coach and Jim Leonhard taking over as defensive coordinator. Buffalo's biggest move was trading for receiver DJ Moore, finally giving Josh Allen a true WR1, while also bolstering their defense with edge rusher Bradley Chubb and several secondary additions. Last season, the Bills had the NFL's best rushing attack, led by James Cook's league-leading 1,621 yards, but their run defense ranked among the league's worst despite an elite pass defense. Allen remains an MVP-caliber dual-threat quarterback, though his passing numbers have dipped over the past two seasons. With Moore now in the mix alongside Khalil Shakir and Dalton Kincaid, and defensive upgrades aimed at fixing their run-stopping issues, Buffalo looks poised to compete.
teams.running_backs: The Bills boasted the best rushing attack in the NFL in 2025, with nearly 160 yards per game. James Cook had an amazing season, leading the NFL in rushing yards with 1621. He had nine games of 100+ rushing yards and added 12 rushing TDs. It’s a seriously potent rushing attack with Josh Allen always a threat with his legs, complemented by the speed and agility of Cook. Cook got paid last year and remains the workhorse RB1 ahead of Ray Davis and Ty Johnson. There has been quite a lot of chat from training camp that Cook will be more involved in the passing game this season, which is exciting news for fantasy coaches. If he can retain that elite rushing output and also add more pass catching he will elevate himself to one of the top running backs in the NFL.
teams.quarterbacks: Josh Allen is arguably the best quarterback in the NFL and is still just 30 years old. He’s been top-5 in MVP voting for five straight seasons and I can’t see that changing this year. He’s coming off a 25 touchdown, 10 interception season but the Bills were really lacking in top receivers last year. Finally they’ve given him a WR1 in DJ Moore who had a decent season in Chicago but still has plenty left in the tank. Allen is a true dual-threat QB, adding 14 rushing touchdowns and 579 rushing yards last year too. The Bills will probably want to rely less on his rushing ability this season and let him throw the ball more. He’s had two straight seasons throwing for less than 400 yards after passing for 4000+ in the previous four seasons. His passing line is set at 3600.5 this year and if he stays healthy he should be surpassing that.
teams.name: BUFFALO BILLS
teams.offseason_changes: It’s a new era in Buffalo after the Bills moved on from head coach Sean McDermott, replacing him with last year’s OC, Joe Brady. They also have a new defensive coordinator in Jim Leonhard (previously at Denver). The big player move was giving up a second-round pick for wide receiver DJ Moore. He’s the best receiver Josh Allen has had since Stefon Diggs left two seasons ago. Buffalo also made some defensive signings, adding edge rusher Bradley Chubb, cornerback Dee Alford and safeties C.J Gardner-Johnson and Geno Stone. Two of their top draft picks (T.J Parker and Davison Igbinosun) also bolster their defense.
teams.prediction_text: I have the Bills marginally winning the AFC East. Josh Allen can win games on his own talent and they’ve added a few nice pieces for him to improve. If their run defense tightens up and DJ Moore performs, they should be a challenger for the Super Bowl.

teams.defence: There aren’t many big name players left on this defense after the departures of Bradley Chubb and Minkah Fitzpatrick. The Dolphins have gone all in on the draft to shore up their defense and look to the future. Corner Chris Johnson is an exciting prospect, taken with pick 27 in the draft. Jacob Rodriguez at linebacker won the Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year and was taken with pick 43 in the draft. It’s a big challenge for defensive coordinator Sean Duggan in his first season with Miami, but he does have a fresh slate to build this defense from scratch.
teams.future_text: While I think the Dolphins will suck, this man certainly doesn’t. Achane has said he wants to lead the NFL in rushing yards this season and I think this is going to be a very run-heavy team with their lack of receiving options. Achane had 1350 rushing yards last season at 5.7 yards per carry and he averages over 5 YPC across his career.
teams.receivers: With both Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle no longer in Miami, there’s no hiding that this is probably the worst receiving corps in the NFL. Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert and Tutu Atwell are all decent players, but none of them would be close to WR1 or maybe even WR2 on many other teams. They did take three different receivers in the draft, but none of those were taken before the third round. They’ll be hoping they can hit on one or two of those guys and there will be plenty of opportunities for them this season as the Dolphins look to the future. We can expect to see plenty of variation in this receiving corps each week and I wouldn’t be relying on any of them for consistent production. There are rumors tight end Greg Dulcich could be the main option. Wait and see what happens in pre-season here before making any major judgements. I would be avoiding betting on most of these players this season.
teams.overview: Miami blew everything up this offseason, firing Mike McDaniel, hiring Jeff Hafley, bringing in a new GM, and shockingly releasing Tua Tagovailoa. Gone too are Tyreek Hill, Bradley Chubb, and Minkah Fitzpatrick, replaced by a league-high 13 draft picks and a $67.5 million gamble on former Packers backup Malik Willis at quarterback. It's a full rebuild with plenty of unknowns. The lone bright spot is De'Von Achane, one of the NFL's most explosive players, coming off a season with 1,350 rushing yards after a strong 2025 campaign despite Miami's struggles. Unfortunately, the receiving corps led by Malik Washington and Jalen Tolbert is arguably the league's worst, with little proven talent to support Willis. The defense is similarly thin, leaning heavily on rookies like cornerback Chris Johnson to rebuild from scratch.
teams.running_backs: De’Von Achane is the Dolphins’ best offensive player and I am a really big fan of his. He is one of the quickest players in the NFL and can break off massive plays both on the ground and in the air. He’s coming off a season with 1350 rushing yards and 488 receiving yards, which are amazing numbers playing for a bad team. He’s a great option for the Dolphins but his ceiling will be limited again due to their lack of general offense. The backups are Jaylen Wright, also an explosive runner, and Ollie Gordon II who was used as the short-yardage and goal-line back at some points last season. The RB room is probably their biggest offensive strength and we can expect some solid numbers from Achane again this year as the Dolphins will likely lean on the run.
teams.quarterbacks: Malik Willis is a bit of a gamble on a $67.5 million deal, but he did show some very promising signs when starting for the Packers. Willis is a powerful athlete who can use his legs and has a bit of a cannon arm too. He had a very impressive start for the Packers against the Ravens last season with 288 passing yards, 1 TD as well as 60 rushing yards and 2 rushing TDs. That showed his potential and he’s a nice fit for this Dolphins team who don’t really have any top receivers left to throw to. Quinn Ewers is Willis’ backup but he’s just not very good, with 3 TDs and 3 interceptions in his four appearances last season.
teams.name: MIAMI DOLPHINS
teams.offseason_changes: The Dolphins blew it up over the off-season. They fired Mike McDaniel, hired Jeff Hafley as head coach, brought in new GM Jon-Erin Sullivan and released QB Tua Tagovailoa. They also moved on from Tyreek Hill, edge rusher Bradley Chubb and safety Minkah Fitzpatrick. In their place: a three-year, $67.5 million deal for former Packers’ backup QB Malik Willis, ex-Texans OC Bobby Slowik as new OC and a league-high 13 draft picks headlined by first-round tackle Kadyn Proctor and cornerback Chris Johnson. There is so much unknown here but you have to respect that they’ve gone all in on the rebuild.
teams.prediction_text: This could get ugly. The Dolphins just don’t have enough talent to compete and they also have a completely new system. It’s going to be a steep learning curve. Having the Patriots and Bills in the Division doesn’t help either.

teams.defence: This is a unit that doesn’t have many massive names, but they play extremely well together. The Patriots allowed the fourth-fewest points per game last season despite having just 19 takeaways all season (12th-fewest in the league). They were ranked in the top 10 in both pass and run defense, proving that it’s a well-rounded unit. Christian Gonzalez is one of the better corners in the league and is still just 24 years old. Vrabel loves a disciplined, physical defense and if they stay healthy, they’ll be a force once again this season.
teams.future_text: Make this line make sense. Yes, Stevenson will still be a big part of the run game, but Henderson has clearly shown he is the more explosive back. He had 911 rushing yards in his rookie season and averaged 5.1 yards per carry. He should improve again and have more trust from Vrabel. Worth a nibble for 1000+ rushing at +340 too.
teams.receivers: The additions of AJ Brown and Romeo Doubs immediately catapult them into the number 1 and 2 options for Drake Maye. Brown has four consecutive seasons with 1000+ yards after he just cleared that mark in his final season with the Eagles. Doubs’ ability shouldn’t be taken lightly either, he had 724 yards last year and will provide a great number 2 option. The Patriots held on to most of their other receivers outside of Stefon Diggs, including Kayshon Boutte, DeMario Douglas and Mack Hollins. All those guys popped up in games last season, combining for just over 1500 yards between them. All of a sudden this is a stacked receiving corps and Drake Maye should help them put up great numbers once again.
teams.overview: The Patriots shocked most people last season with an amazing run to the Super Bowl. They then made a splash by trading for wide receiver AJ Brown, finally giving Drake Maye the true WR1 he lacked during his stellar 2025 season, while also adding Romeo Doubs to round out the receiving corps. Last season, Maye finished second in MVP voting, throwing for 4,394 yards and 31 touchdowns despite having just one 1,000-yard receiver, and the Patriots' disciplined defense allowed the fourth-fewest points in the league. This year, Maye inherits a genuinely stacked receiving group featuring Brown, Doubs, and holdovers like Kayshon Boutte, while TreVeyon Henderson looks poised to take over the backfield after a strong rookie season alongside Rhamondre Stevenson. The defense, anchored by young corner Christian Gonzalez, remains a well-rounded, physical unit under Mike Vrabel.
teams.running_backs: The Patriots had the sixth-ranked rushing attack last season, with 128.9 yards per game. Rhamondre Stevenson compiled over 600 yards and he formed a nice partnership with rookie TreVeyon Henderson who had over 900 rushing yards. Henderson is the future of this backfield and although he didn’t have the full trust of Vrabel last season, he should be the main man in 2026. He showed his ceiling in a couple of games last year, with two performances of 140+ rushing yards and 2+ touchdowns. Stevenson is the bigger back and can be used on short yardage situations, but Henderson is much more explosive and also arguably a better pass-catcher. Mike Vrabel does like to run with the hot hand at times so expect to see both guys put up decent numbers this season.
teams.quarterbacks: Drake Maye had a remarkable season in just his second year in the NFL, finishing second in MVP voting behind Matthew Stafford. The Patriots had the second-most passing yards per game in the NFL despite having just one receiver with 1000+ yards (Stefon Diggs). Maye put up serious numbers: 4394 passing yards, 31 touchdowns, 450 rushing yards and just 8 interceptions. Maye is a serious threat with his legs too and if he can improve again this season, he will cement himself as one of the best players in the league. It will be great to see how he goes with AJ Brown, who will undoubtedly expect a lot of targets. One of the Patriots’ strengths last season was their ability to spread the ball out between receivers. I’m looking forward to seeing Maye improve again this year.
teams.name: NEW ENGLAND PATRIOTS
teams.offseason_changes: The blockbuster trade for the Patriots this off-season was trading a first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder to Philadelphia for wide receiver AJ Brown. Drake Maye now has a true WR1 which he somewhat lacked in his breakout 2025 season. The Patriots also signed WR Romeo Doubs from Green Bay, so it’s a new look receiving corps. They also added Caleb Lomu and Gabe Jacas early in the draft to shore up the offensive line and pass rush. It was an aggressive off-season and the Patriots clearly think they can challenge for the Super Bowl once again.
teams.prediction_text: I think there will be some regression from last year’s 14-3 record and Super Bowl appearance. They have a much harder schedule than last year. I am still a big fan of this team though and they’ve arguably gotten better in the off-season with the addition of AJ Brown and Drake Maye going into his third year.

teams.defence: It was a historically bad season for the Jets’ defense in 2025, recording just four takeaways (fewest by any team since 1940) and zero interceptions. They ranked 25th in total defense and that was a clear focus to improve on this season. The arrivals of veterans Demario Davis and Minkah Fitzpatrick should help, plus pick 2 David Bailey who helps the pass-rush alongside Will McDonald IV. Head coach Aaron Glenn is a defensive minded coach and he’s under some pressure this year to make the scheme click. Surely we see a few more interceptions from the Jets this year…
teams.future_text: Before an injury-interrupted 2025 season, Wilson had 1000+ yards in all three NFL seasons prior. He also had some terrible QB play then. Whilst Geno Smith is not much better, he is capable of supporting a true WR1 and I think that will be the case this year. We should see a big season for Wilson.
teams.receivers: This receiver room is looking pretty exciting for 2026 after an injection of talent in the draft. The Jets took tight end Kenyon Sadiq with pick 16 and he’s a serious athlete, running the 40-yard dash in 4.39 seconds at the combine, the fastest mark by a tight end since 2003. He’s a 6-3, 241 beast who will get plenty of mismatches. They took him with the pick acquired from the Sauce Gardner trade with the Colts last year. The Jets still have 2025 second rounder Mason Taylor who also showed some promising signs last year, so there’s plenty of potential for them at the tight end position. With the 30th pick in the draft the Jets took wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr from Indiana, trading up three spots to get him. He’s another good athlete who is dangerous after the catch and he’ll get every opportunity to prove himself in a season where the Jets look to the future. Garrett Wilson is WR1 and I’m a big fan – he had 1000+ receiving yards in his first three NFL seasons (with bad QBs) before getting injured last year. He’ll benefit from a more competent QB in Geno Smith. Adonai Mitchell also has a lot of speed and big-play ability but has had issues with drops. He’s a former second-round pick and I still think he has plenty of potential.
teams.overview: After a historically bad 3-14 season, the Jets brought in Geno Smith as a bridge quarterback and used premium draft picks on edge rusher David Bailey, tight end Kenyon Sadiq, and receiver Omar Cooper Jr. They also loaded up on veteran defensive help, adding Demario Davis, Minkah Fitzpatrick, and Joseph Ossai after a defense that recorded the fewest takeaways since 1940. Breece Hall gets locked in long-term after a strong 2025 and should thrive behind better quarterback play, while Garrett Wilson looks primed for a bounce-back season now that he's got a competent passer throwing him the ball. The rookie tight ends and receivers add real upside to a young, exciting offensive core. Head coach Aaron Glenn enters year two under pressure to fix a historically porous defense.
teams.running_backs: The Jets have committed to running back Breece Hall after signing him to a three-year contract extension worth up to $45.75 million, with $29 million guaranteed. There were a lot of trade rumours around Hall last season but he’s now locked in as a part of their future. Hall had a solid 2025 season in a very bad team, recording over 1400 total scrimmage yards and five touchdowns. The Jets can’t get much worse than they were last year, so I’m expecting Hall to put up some solid numbers in 2026 and I wouldn’t be surprised to see him finish with 1500+ scrimmage yards. Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis return to the team as well. Neither were overly efficient last year but the Jets’ situation certainly didn’t help them either.
teams.quarterbacks: It was a very ugly season at QB for the Jets, who started three different guys across the season. They put up just 140 passing yards per game, easily the lowest mark in the NFL. Geno Smith should improve those numbers but he’s not the future for this team. It’s a decent addition for the Jets who really just need a bridge QB before hopefully finding a player in the draft. They did select QB Cade Klubnik with pick 110 and actually traded up 18 spots to take him there. He wasn’t expected to go until the later rounds so the Jets clearly see some potential in him. He’ll almost definitely start as the backup to Smith to start the season but we could see him get reps later, likely once the Jets start tanking.
teams.name: NEW YORK JETS
teams.offseason_changes: A huge amount of change after a historically bad 3-14 season for the Jets. Geno Smith has been signed at QB and the Jets used the number 2 overall pick on Texas Tech edge rusher David Bailey. They also added two more first round picks in tight end Kenyon Sadiq and receiver Omar Cooper Jr. The key was adding veteran talent around this new young core and they did that, bringing in linebacker Demario Davis, safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, corner Nahshon Wright and edge rushers Joseph Ossai and Kingsley Enagbare. Head coach Aaron Glenn is in his second year and will need the team to show improvement.
teams.prediction_text: Look away Jets fans. Whilst this is the equal worst record I have predicted for any team this season, I think there will be some positives. They’ve drafted some nice talent and this is clearly a bridge year before hopefully drafting a good quarterback at the end of the season.

picks.description: Despite throwing 41 touchdowns and over 4,100 yards last season, Lamar couldn't retain his MVP title. It was the first time he surpassed 4,000 passing yards and he only threw 4 interceptions as well. I suspect there was some voter fatigue but that shouldn't be an issue for him this season. The Baltimore offense remains one of the best in the NFL and the addition of DeAndre Hopkins gives Lamar another weapon.
